finalText:
Five small files, all in `src/` — no tests, no config, no package.json even. It's a minimal HTTP API for users and orders.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  server.js -->|checks token| auth.js
  server.js --> routes.js
  routes.js -->|GET requests| cache.js
  cache.js --> store.js
  routes.js -->|POST requests| store.js
```

- **`server.js`** — the front door. Every request must carry a `Bearer <userId>.<sig>` header checked by `auth.js`; no valid token, no further than a 401.
- **`auth.js`** — signs and checks tokens with HMAC-SHA256, using `AUTH_SECRET` from the environment (falls back to `'dev-secret'` if unset).
- **`routes.js`** — a small table matching `METHOD path` to a handler. `GET /users` and `GET /orders` read through the cache; `POST /orders` writes straight to the store.
- **`store.js`** — the actual data, kept in memory. Stands in for a real database, and every record expires 15 minutes after its last write.
- **`cache.js`** — a 256-entry LRU sitting in front of the store, just to catch repeated reads. No expiry of its own.

One thing worth knowing before you touch this: the comment in `routes.js` says writes "invalidate the affected keys," but `putOrder` never actually clears the cache. So after someone posts a new order, `GET /orders` can keep serving the old cached list until it ages out or gets bumped from the LRU.
